home.headline: Build focus you can measure.
home.subhead: Take a 3-minute reaction test, try short practices, and see which ones beat plain rest for you. Free, private, no account.
home.loopSubtitle: Add a behavioural measure alongside your own impressions.
home.loop1Desc: Take a 3-minute reaction-time test (PVT-B) in your browser to measure sustained attention and alertness lapses.
home.loop2Desc: Engage with structured focus sessions, breath pacing, and quiet rest—each clearly tagged with its empirical support.
home.loop3Desc: Run self-directed A/B experiments comparing an active technique against quiet rest to test individual efficacy.
home.evidenceStripTitle: Every tip shows how strong its evidence is.
home.evidenceStripSub: We distinguish high-replication findings from preliminary pilots and claims that lack supporting evidence.
home.privacyTitle: No account. Your data stays on your device.
home.privacyDesc: Zero trackers, zero remote databases, and no login walls. Your results live in your browser's private local storage.
home.faqSubtitle: Transparent answers regarding methodology, privacy, and evidence.
home.faq1A: Yes. FocusLab is 100% free and open-source. There are no subscriptions, paywalls, tracking scripts, or advertisements.
home.faq2A: All data stays entirely on your own device in your browser local storage. Nothing is sent to an external server or cloud database.
home.faq3Q: Is FocusLab a medical or diagnostic tool?
home.faq3A: No. FocusLab is an educational self-tracking project. It does not diagnose ADHD or other clinical conditions and does not offer medical advice.
home.faq4Q: Why use a reaction-time test to measure focus?
home.faq4A: Subjective focus ratings are easily biased by expectations. Brief reaction-time testing (PVT-B) provides a behavioral measure of attention lapses directly in your browser.
home.faq5A: Claims are evaluated across 5 transparent tiers (Strong to Not Supported) derived directly from peer-reviewed meta-analyses for the specific outcome named.
onboarding.goalTitle: What is your primary focus goal?
onboarding.goalSub: FocusLab adapts to your current context with zero tracking or user accounts.
onboarding.obstacleSub: Choose the challenge you face most frequently when trying to concentrate.
onboarding.obsPhoneDesc: Urge to check feeds and notifications
onboarding.obsTiredDesc: Mental exhaustion or lack of alertness
onboarding.obsNoiseDesc: Uncontrolled sensory distractions in your space
onboarding.recsSub: Based on your obstacle, here are evidence-labelled tools to try first:
check.title: Focus Check
check.introSub: A 3-minute reaction-time measurement (PVT-B) to assess sustained alertness and lapses.
check.introP1: This test measures sustained vigilance and reaction speed. It is an informal personal benchmark, not an ADHD diagnostic or clinical screening.
check.introP2: Take about 3 minutes in a quiet space without distractions. Use the same device and browser each time for valid self-comparison.
check.ratingsSub: Record how you feel right now before beginning the reaction test.
check.testInstruction: Keep your eyes on the box. Respond as quickly as possible.
check.resultsSub: Here is your attention performance summary for this session.
footer.notice: Notice: FocusLab is an educational self-experimentation tool and does not provide medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment. All data stays in your browser.
sounds.tryThenTestBody: Background noise may aid attention in higher-distraction environments while distracting in quiet spaces. Use the secondary button above to schedule a 10-run self-experiment against silence.
